hints.title: Tree Partition into Three Components
hints.text: Removing node x disconnects the tree into at most three independent branches: left child subtree, right child subtree, and the parent branch.

hints.title: Subtree Size Calculation
hints.text: Compute the size of node x left child subtree (left_size) and right child subtree (right_size).

hints.title: Winning Majority Threshold
hints.text: The parent component has size n - (left_size + right_size + 1). Player 2 can win if and only if the maximum of these three component sizes is strictly greater than n // 2.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def btreeGameWinningMove(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], n: int, x: int) -> bool:
        left_cnt = 0
        right_cnt = 0
        
        def count_nodes(node):
            nonlocal left_cnt, right_cnt
            if not node:
                return 0
            l = count_nodes(node.left)
            r = count_nodes(node.right)
            if node.val == x:
                left_cnt = l
                right_cnt = r
            return 1 + l + r
        
        count_nodes(root)
        parent_cnt = n - (left_cnt + right_cnt + 1)
        return max(left_cnt, right_cnt, parent_cnt) > n // 2
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating sequential coloring moves game-tree fashion is unnecessary when node selection partitions all accessible vertices.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single depth traversal counts subtree sizes in linear time and stack space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that Player 2 can pick an immediate neighbor of x to block Player 1 from that entire branch.
complexity.notes: Total node count n is guaranteed to be odd.
